claim_being_audited: The actor claims the current release can be certified now because aggregate launch readiness exceeds the threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, with the subgroup regression handled narrowly through documentation and monitoring context.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if material segment weaknesses are either disclosed before launch or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
Contextual evidence such as prior approvals or informal monitoring comments cannot substitute for current evidence satisfying those requirements.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model-card or release documentation showing the retirement plan servicing limitation is explicitly disclosed for this launch.
Provide an approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the retirement plan servicing regression for the current release.
Provide evidence that the current retrieval configuration and current eval batch were reviewed and approved for certification under the present policy standard.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification.
Admissible evidence shows a current material subgroup regression in retirement plan servicing below the warning threshold.
Admissible evidence also shows there is no reviewed mitigation, no owner acceptance, and no disclosure language attached to the release record.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration and eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release support requirement.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure the separate policy condition for material segment weaknesses.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification is presently supportable is not supported because the required disclosure or approved mitigation for the current subgroup weakness is missing.
Any implication that informal post-launch monitoring is an adequate substitute for approved mitigation or disclosure is unsupported by the policy text.
Any implication that prior approval for the model family materially supports the current certification decision beyond background context is overstated.
